Mr. Sainovic was treated deferentially by the other members throughout. General Vasiljevic said Mr. Sainovic presided over this meeting. This meeting of the leading members of the MUP and the VJ in Kosovo. And he said, in these circumstances, he, General Vasiljevic, could only conclude that Sainovic must have been appointed to this position by Mr. Milutinovic -- sorry, by Mr. Milosevic, because it was a position of such high power and control, and that he would have reported to Mr. Milosevic. The meeting began with a briefing by General Lukic, and if you look at the briefing what he said about the briefing, the briefing involved detail of activities of an underground by the MUP. After this, General Lazarevic gave his report and used a map which showed distribution of forces, et cetera. Again, if you look at this, you can assess the level of detail that these leading members of the force of the FRY and Serbia were addressing and reporting to Mr. Sainovic. Following that, General Pavkovic spoke. After this, Sainovic spoke and said, and I'm quoting now: "Okay. Do as you have planned." Then he said the remaining terrorist groups were to be destroyed in the next three to four days, and that the organisation of activities in the field and cooperation between the MUP and the army is to be improved. According to General Vasiljevic, nobody stood at attention to receive that as an order but Sainovic's word was last, and the meeting disbanded. It was, in General Vasiljevic's estimation, a meeting which lasted 20 minutes, dealt with details of events that occurred in the last 24 hours, including combat operations, and therefore according to General Vasiljevic would have been something in the nature of a daily or certainly a meeting that was called frequently because of the atmosphere at the meeting, the topics and the time it lasted. In this evidence, there is material, it is respectfully submitted, that rebuts and disposes of the submissions of Mr. Sainovic that I just outlined under those eight heads, except for the last one, that people spoke about Mr. Sainovic's conduct with approval. Where there is other evidence on these several matters, Mr. Sainovic submitted that the evidence was that -- Mr. Fila submitted that the evidence was that Mr. Sainovic was a middle man who conveyed positions of high-ranking officials. As I indicated, this is neither unusual or inconsistent. This is part of the Prosecution's case that he conveyed orders, et cetera, from Mr. Milosevic. The joint criminal enterprise involved various parties who played their own part led by Mr. Milosevic, and some persons had more than one role. And Mr. Fila's position on this may well have been a misunderstanding of the evidence that he cited, that is of Mr. Merovci. That evidence is at page 8535 of the transcript as a matter for this Court. It seems that Mr. Merovci is saying that on some occasions, in his opinion, Mr. Sainovic was a person who came frequently and announced meetings. In a way, he could have been a person who acted in a capacity as an envoy, who conveyed opinions of higher ranks, but it was not -- but nothing from his testimony goes to suggest that he was saying that this was exclusively Mr. Sainovic's role. There is, as far as the second head is concerned, significant evidence that Mr. Sainovic was Mr. Milosevic's representative in Kosovo. Mr. Surroi testified at 4547 of the transcript to 4548, that Mr. Sainovic was clearly Mr. Milosevic's most trusted man in Kosovo. Mr. Naumann testified much to the same -- much to the same -- in the same manner. He testified that Mr. Sainovic was introduced to him as a Deputy Prime Minister and the man responsible for Kosovo. And he also signed the 25th of October agreement or record, meeting record, as the one responsible for Kosovo. See also the evidence of Mr. DZ, P2508 at paragraph 201; Mr. Vollebaek at 9508 of the transcript; Mr. Kickert, 11235 of the transcript. Mr. Merovci testified that both he and Dr. Rugova knew that Mr. Sainovic's position as one of the persons designated by -- sorry, that both he and Mr. -- and Dr. Rugova knew that Sainovic was one of the persons designated by Mr. Milosevic to have responsibility for Kosovo. That's P2588. And so did Dr. Rugova in his statement. Similarly, General Loncar, in his statement, concluded that from the information he had, Sainovic was in charge of Kosovo on Mr. Milosevic's instructions. And that is P2521, paragraph 38. And there is interspersed in the evidence of Mr. -- of Ambassador Petritsch many statements that Mr. Sainovic held this role. He further said that there is no evidence that in 1999, Mr. Sainovic was head of the Joint Command. And in addition to the evidence about -- the evidence from General Vasiljevic, there is other evidence. Ljubinko Cvetic testified that as far as he knew, as a head of one of the Secretariats of the interior for Kosovo, Mr. Sainovic was head of the Joint Command. And this is at T8078 -- at transcript 8078. And Mr. Lukic made a similar statement in his interview, P4 -- P948 at page 106. There is an exhibit which I'll get to, which details about 60 meetings of the Joint Command in 1998, in which Mr. Sainovic attended as a head. I'll get to it. It's P1498, meetings from the 22nd of July 1998 to the 30th of October 1998, where Sainovic is identified as present and participating in most of those meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you say 60 meetings?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: 69 separate meetings. Lest it be said that Sainovic may just have participated or attended for even a single occasion after the 24th of March 1999, and as that was a focus, a thrust of the submissions in this regard, that we cannot by analogy refer to 98 and assume the same situation occurred in 1998 in 1999. There are other meetings in 1999 after the 24th of March. There was one on the 4th of April 1999, and this was a MUP meeting, and this is referred to at P1989, and in those minutes, it is said that federal Deputy Prime Minister Nikola Sainovic joined the work. And it refers to so many of the directives that Mr. Sainovic gave at that meeting. In other words, he's giving directives to senior members of the MUP in Kosovo on the 4th of April 1999. Mr. Cvetic as the commander or Secretary of the Interior was also present at that meeting and he said that Mr. Sainovic assisted and requested and asked all the police present to conduct themselves highly professionally, et cetera, in carrying out their duties, not to mistreat anyone or committing any sort of misdemeanour. He also gave a variety of instructions to the police and also said operations that had been planned to take place on or up until the 4th of April were to be concluded by the end of that day and they were to move on to other tasks. So he's directing them as to the timing of their task. He's giving them directions that's what they were supposed to be doing in the field. It meant that they were to make changes and camouflage themselves against NATO attacks, et cetera. 7th of May 1999, another MUP staff meeting. The minutes are P1996. Mr. Sainovic took part according to the minutes, addressing the group at the very start. The meeting was chaired by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic opened the meeting but immediately gave the floor to Mr. Sainovic who proceeded to make a speech about the MUP VJ coordination, stating that all detachments of the PJP Special Police units would return to their Secretariats and in cooperation with the VJ work on destroying the remaining terrorist groups. Similarly, there is a meeting on the 17th of May. The minutes -- sorry, this is described in General Vasiljevic's testimony in the Milosevic case. That's P2589, at transcript 15999 to 1600 [sic]. The next submission by learned counsel, Mr. Fila, was that the Joint Command or the documents referring to the Joint Command, if the documents are authentic, are VJ documents and they refer solely to army units. If we look, Your Honours, at three of those documents, and I believe there are many -- not necessarily many but there are others. P2809 is an order for the engagement of the Serbian MUP in the Pristina Corps area of responsibility and that is dated the 25th of April 1999. This is a Pristina Corps command document but it speaks about coordinated activities with the MUP. But the three documents I wish to refer to, which highlight the role of the Joint Command in ordering and coordinating the activities of the VJ and the MUP is -- begins with P2015 the Joint Command order of the 23rd of March 1999, in which there is, among other things, an order to "provide assistance to the MUP in crushing and destroying Siptar terrorist forces in Orahovac, Suva Reka and Velika Krusa sector," and it directly refers to the coordinated assault, if I may, of both VJ and MUP forces. I respectfully remind the Tribunal that in those areas, at that time, there are significant uncharged offences of murder and deportations committed by the forces of FRY and Serbia. Orahovac, Suva Reka. It also specifically orders 549th Motorised Brigade to perform tasks in Orahovac and Prizren at that time, and these are also two sites identified in the indictment and this is item, page 3 of P2015. And it states that the Joint Command from Pristina section shall command and control all forces during combat operations. P1981 implements on the brigade level the Joint Command order, I mentioned before and it is signed by Colonel Bozidar Delic, who we have heard about in this case before. And again demonstrates that the VJ, the MUP and the PJP operated joint actions in the villages identified in the indictment, at the relevant time identified in the indictment. P1995 is an analysis of the operation of the 549th Motorised Brigade in routing the KLA and lifting the blockade on Suva Reka as ordered by the Joint Command and by Colonel Delic, and it again shows that the operation in Suva Reka and Orahovac were conducted by forces under the Joint Command and forces of the MUP and VJ. Learned counsel, Mr. Fila also submitted that the MUP of Serbia was fully under the jurisdiction of the republic. There is evidence demonstrating, it is submitted, that the MUP of Serbia was not only under the jurisdiction of the republic but was also resubordinated to the VJ for operational purposes and in these activities or these operations, they were under the command of a Joint Command. P1920, I'd ask Your Honours to look at that. P14 -- well, I should mention that it is an order, issued by General Ojdanic to the 3rd Army, dated the 29th of May 1999 and it shows the subordination of the MUP to the VJ, at least for the purposes of these operations. P1483, demonstrates that for operations, those operations that are discussed there, the forces of the MUP were resubordinated to the VJ. It also states that forces of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and civilian Defence shall be placed under the command of the 3rd Army during the operation and they shall be used exclusively by your decision. Similarly, an order from General Ojdanic on the 18th of April 1999 also subordinates MUP forces to the VJ. And it says the authority for the subordination, Article 17 of the Law on Defence. P2821 is to a similar effect. General Vasiljevic testified to the same effect, without going into the details. This is at T1590 -- T15991 of the transcript. He also said in his statement, at paragraph 43, and that's P2594, "Although they" - that is the MUP - "were not formally part of the Supreme Command the MUP was practically under the control of along the vertical line that went through the Minister of Interior of Serbia and then further on in depth," and he said that this is a legacy of the period when Mr. Milosevic was president of Serbia and as such had more direct authority over the Serbian MUP. In this regard, I'd also refer the Court to P2809, an order signed by General Lazarevic. The next submission by Mr. Fila was that there was no evidence establishing a chain of command of which Mr. Sainovic was a part or demonstrating a vertical chain of command involving Mr. Sainovic. I'd again refer the Court to Mr. -- to General Vasiljevic's testimony that notwithstanding the fact that Mr. Sainovic was not an appointed member of the police or the army, notwithstanding the fact that he had apparently very little de jure responsibility for these organs, that he attended the meetings and he commanded them; he exercised control over them. And again, that is demonstrated in P1989, the minutes of the meeting of the 4th of April 1999 of the MUP leadership. I think my colleague Mr. Hannis referred to Mr. Perisic's letter, so I won't go into the details of that, but Mr. Perisic -- sorry, General Perisic complained about the alternative chain of command where Mr. Sainovic was involved, as it were, in directing VJ units. Mr. Cvetic testified that Mr. Sainovic was entrusted with the coordination of the military and the police. That's at 8124 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The witness you've just referred to, could you spell his name, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: C-v-e-t-i-c.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's been repeated with a different spelling several times but that should clarify any doubt in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There is the evidence of Mr. Panic in this regard which I will not quote, but that is at T6371, and I have various references to General Vasiljevic. General Vasiljevic's testimony is replete with this sort of reference. Mr. Fila submitted that there is sufficient evidence -- that there was no evidence demonstrating that Mr. Sainovic could have and, in fact, did know about the crimes alleged in the indictment. In this issue of knowledge, again, naturally, Your Honours would have to -- with -- and I know, examine all the evidence of all the meetings that he attended, assess the evidence in respect to the massive crimes that were going on on the ground, and come to an appropriate conclusion. The Prosecution submits that the only conclusion, even if that is not necessary at this stage, but the only conclusion is that he must have known about what was going on on the ground. And in support of that, not only the general inference that somebody in his position receiving these reports, travelling around Kosovo, must have known about what was happening, there are also minutes of meetings, for example, P1.000, the minutes of the SDC meeting on the 20th of December 1998, in which Sainovic is recorded as reporting to the SDC on the activities of the VJ and the MUP in Kosovo, and the efficiency of their cooperation while in operation in Kosovo. General Loncar testified, and Your Honours can draw necessary inferences from this testimony, that Mr. Sainovic insisted on being informed of the activities in Kosovo and established strict communication channels to facilitate the process, and these communication channels involved himself, General Loncar, General Lukic, General Pavkovic, General Lazarevic. This is transcript 7649 to 7654. General Naumann testified that on the 19th of January 1999, he gave Sainovic a list of the violations of the October agreement, including issues of excessive force. In addition, there is P400, a letter -- if I may just have a moment to make an inquiry?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will -- sorry, I will check the facts for the submission I intended to make and I'll get back to you. It is possible that the document might not have been received into evidence. As a matter of fact, it was received into evidence on the 10th of October 2006, and this is Exhibit P400, which is a letter of the 26th of March 1999, just about the time when the -- when many of the serious offences were being committed, and this is from former ICTY Prosecutor Louise Arbour to Mr. Sainovic, and the Prosecutor -- the then Prosecutor made references to the escalating violence in Kosovo and expressed concerns about the serious violations of international humanitarian law. And Mr. Vasiljevic, General Vasiljevic, in his statement indicated that at the meeting of the 17th of May 1999, it was reported that crimes committed by the VJ and volunteers and those responsible for crimes in Podujevo, were moved on to elsewhere until Biljani where they committed other crimes. I'm sorry, it was reported that the crimes committed by the VJ and by volunteers in Podujevo were committed by persons who were moved on to other places, and this is at P2594, paragraphs 63 to 72. I will complete that submission as to when and where Mr. Sainovic would have received that report when we resume, Your Honour. I -- well, it's a matter really for the Court, but I'm wondering it this is a convenient moment since I'll have to return anyway.
